title: INCIBE-CERT rates D-Link DIR-600L end-of-life router flaw critical: unauthenticated stack overflow, public proof of concept
place: Madrid, Spain (INCIBE-CERT, publisher of the advisory)
geo_basis: advisory publisher; the flaw affects devices worldwide
summary: INCIBE-CERT rates CVE-2026-129354 critical (importance 5). In the D-Link DIR-600L router, hardware revision B, firmware 2.17b02, the hnap_main function does not check the length of the HTTP SOAPAction header, so a remote unauthenticated attacker can overflow a stack buffer. A published proof of concept crashes the CGI process in an emulated setup. INCIBE lists exploitation as not observed. D-Link says revision B is end of life.
plain: INCIBE-CERT says a remote attacker without a login can overflow a memory buffer in the D-Link DIR-600L router, hardware revision B. D-Link says that revision is end of life, and a public proof of concept exists.
exec: INCIBE-CERT rates the flaw critical, notes a public proof of concept and lists exploitation as not observed; D-Link says revision B is end of life.
action: INCIBE-CERT recommends replacing the router with a supported model and, in the meantime, disabling remote administration and restricting the management interface to a trusted network.
impact: Remote buffer overflow without authentication on an unsupported router; no fix will be issued.

validation.note: INCIBE-CERT (Spain's national CERT) advisory INCIBE-2026-896, read in full on 25 Nov after earlier load failures; it relays D-Link's end-of-life statement. No second publisher read.
